Package com.privatechain.network.peer

Class PeerStore

java.lang.Object
com.privatechain.network.peer.PeerStore
public final class PeerStore extends Object
Thread-safe in-memory store for known Peer instances.

PeerStore acts as the single source of truth for the peer list maintained by PeerManager. It provides atomic put/get/remove operations and supports snapshot queries. In a production deployment this class would back its map with a persistent store (e.g., a small embedded JSON file or LevelDB entry) so that the node can reconnect to previously known peers after a restart without relying solely on seed peers.

Thread safety

All methods are safe for concurrent use. Reads and writes are serialized via ConcurrentHashMap which provides lock-free reads and striped-lock writes.

Key design decision

Peers are keyed by nodeId (not by host:port) because a peer's IP address can change on reconnect while its cryptographic identity stays constant. This ensures that a reconnected peer replaces its stale entry rather than creating a duplicate.

Since:
1.0.0

  • Method Details

    • put

      public void put(Peer peer)
      Inserts or replaces a peer entry keyed by Peer.getNodeId().

      If a peer with the same node ID already exists (e.g., reconnecting on a new IP address), the old entry is overwritten atomically.

      Parameters:
      peer - the peer to store (non-null)
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if peer is null

    • remove

      public void remove(String nodeId)
      Removes a peer from the store by node ID.

      No-op if the node ID is not present.

      Parameters:
      nodeId - the node ID to remove (non-null, non-blank)
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if nodeId is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if nodeId is blank

    • getAll

      public List<Peer> getAll()
      Returns a point-in-time snapshot of all known peers.

      Modifications to the returned list do not affect the store. Peers are returned in an unspecified order; callers that need a deterministic order should sort the list themselves.

      Returns:
      unmodifiable list of all current peers

      Returns:
